gen-nixie-one-fs-supreme: Outline-like letters of one constant stroke give Nixie One its retro-tech glow, with open curves and clear gaps. Supreme sits under it as a heavier, lower band of text.
gen-nixie-one-general-sans: Nixie One has a nostalgic, retro-tech look, its open curves and constant stroke leaving clear gaps all along each letter. General Sans then flows on smoothly, its tall x-height filling each line.
gen-nixie-one-gf-orbit: Retro-tech glow on top, spaced-out letters below. Nixie One is best at open curves and a constant stroke, while Orbit is best at keeping each stem, bowl and tail rope-consistent.
gen-nixie-one-gf-science-gothic: Retro-tech and open, Nixie One keeps a constant stroke from top to baseline. Science Gothic keeps its stroke ends far apart and every stroke uniform, so reading goes one letter at a time.
gen-nixie-one-work-sans: Open curves and a constant stroke give Nixie One its retro-tech look. Work Sans stands beside it with a high mean line and c tips kept well apart, which feels modern next to that nostalgia.
gen-orbitron-archivo: Neon-tube precision, every letter spread wide along the line. Orbitron earns its keep big and short, while Archivo brings outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height to the running text.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-abeezee: Pinned-apart letters like cut-outs give Press Start 2P its fun, retro bite. ABeeZee settles into a soft, featureless hum across the paragraph, with terminals that stop well short of each stem.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-aldrich: Cut-out letters pinned far apart mark Press Start 2P, with a faint weight change you only catch up close. Aldrich brings a single thick thread of cupped, tall-set letters.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati reads big and open, its lowercase rivalling the capitals and its c gaping wide beneath Press Start 2P. The cut-out spacing up top is the part you remember most.
